claim.short: Driver decomposition of the human_skin_transfer.py finding (gastrocnemius +0.826 vs skin -0.665 Spearman against human i4_skin NES). On the 25 shared pathways (22 Reactome + 3 Hallmark), the contrast is driven by a translation/proteostasis family (11 pathways) where mouse gastrocnemius matches the human-skin down-regulation 10/11 times and mouse skin matches only 1/11. Leading-edge intersection across mouse gastrocnemius missions for the top 5 r-lifting pathways is dominated by ribosomal-protein genes (Rpl10a/Rpl13/Rpl14/.../Rps*, plus mitochondrial Mrpl*/Mrps* and the universal Fau small-subunit constituent), consistent with the classical spaceflight muscle proteostasis-suppression signature transferring onto human Inspiration4 skin biopsy.

inputs.notes: Same local mouse fGSEA cache as human_skin_transfer.py, with the leadingEdge_str column consumed for the gene-level intersection. c2cgp/c5bp expansions are HPC-only and absent here.
Identical file as in bridge_human_skin_transfer; the human side does not carry a leadingEdge column, so the gene-level intersection is mouse-only.

validation.notes: Exploratory local-only run; promotion to hpc_validated requires the same c2cgp/c5bp HPC expansion called out in bridge_human_skin_transfer. Family-level conclusions are expected to hold at higher n because the translation/proteostasis signature is already saturated at this n; per-pathway leave-one-out values will sharpen and additional non-translation families (e.g., C2 chemical-perturbation programs) may enter the overlap.
